title: Prudential Regulation Authority Business Plan 2026/27
summary: The PRA Business Plan 2026/27 outlines supervisory priorities and regulatory reforms for UK banks and insurers, including continued Basel III implementation, liquidity reporting requirements for insurers, and work on bank liquidity rules responding to faster bank runs experienced in the US in 2023. The plan confirms continued focus on safety and soundness alongside efficiency objectives.
key_points: The PRA regulates 1,254 firms: 686 deposit-takers and 568 insurers of all types
In January 2026, rules were published implementing remaining Basel III elements, with implementation proceeding through 2026/27
A simplified capital regime for small domestic banks will be fully in place from January 2027
Work on bank liquidity aims to respond to faster bank runs experienced mainly in the US in 2023
Liquidity reporting for insurers was recently introduced and will be embedded in 2026/27
The PRA will engage on ring-fencing regime reforms with HM Treasury
Periodic Summary Meetings moving to a two-year cycle for all firms
why_it_matters: This business plan signals the PRA's supervisory priorities and upcoming regulatory changes affecting UK banks and insurers. Market participants in UK financial services should note the timeline for Basel III completion and simplified capital regime for smaller banks, as these affect capital requirements and competitive dynamics between large and small lenders.
market_structure_context: The document references work on bank liquidity requirements aimed at addressing faster bank run dynamics observed in US regional banks in 2023, suggesting potential implications for deposit competition and bank funding structures. However, the business plan itself is a forward-looking work programme rather than a market-moving announcement.
